newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's 97 debt/GDP reduction to exceed plans.
newsitem.headline: Spain's 97 debt/GDP reduction to exceed plans.

text.p: Spanish Budget Secretary Jose Folgado said on Monday that the actual reduction of debt to gross domestic product in 1997 would surpass that planned for in the budget.
The debt/GDP objective for 1997 is 67.2 percent, down from 67.5 percent in 1996.
"It is going to be clearly better than in the budget," Folgado told Reuters in an interview.

Folgado said Spain had budgeted for receipts of 450 billion pesetas from privatisations, all of which would be used to retire debt. In addition, savings in interest rate payments as official rates declined would also be devoted to retiring debt.
Official rates declined to 6.25 percent at the end of 1996 from nine percent at the beginning of the year.
Any additional receipts would be devoted to building up infrastructure, Folgado said.
Telefonica, whose remaining 20.9 percent stake is currently being privatised, has estimated receipts of 650 billion pesetas from the sale if the share price is 3,300 pesetas.
On midday Monday, the share price was trading at 3,265 pesetas.

Income of upcoming privatisations, such as Repsol SA which depends on another state agency, will be used to cover old industrial debts and to help restructure deficit-making state industries, he said.
